origin.description: Shapiro-Francia test of the composite hypothesis of normality.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector with between 5 and 5000 non-missing values. Missing values are dropped.

origin.details: W is the squared correlation of the ordered sample with qnorm(ppoints(n, a = 3/8)). The p-value is Royston's normal approximation to log(1 - W). A constant sample makes cor warn that the standard deviation is zero and both W and the p-value are NA.
origin.value: An htest list with statistic W, the p-value, the method, and the data name.

translation.description: Shapiro-Francia test of the composite hypothesis of normality.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric values with between 5 and 5000 non-missing entries. NaN is dropped.

translation.details: W is the squared correlation of the ordered sample with qnorm(ppoints(n, a=3/8)). The p-value is Royston's normal approximation to log(1 - W). A constant sample warns that the standard deviation is zero and both W and the p-value are NaN. The quantile is SciPy's normal ppf.
translation.value: An htest object with statistic W, the p-value, the method, and the data name.
translation.example:
from nortest import sf_test

x = [2.1, 3.4, float("nan"), 1.2, 5.6, 4.0, 3.3, 2.8, 6.1, 1.9, float("nan"), 4.4]
print(sf_test(x), end="")
